task_description: Write a method in Dafny to find the median of two sorted lists of same size.
specification_response:
Method Signature:
    method MedianOfTwoSortedLists(a: seq<int>, b: seq<int>) returns (median: real)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The input sequences a and b are both sorted and of the same length
- The returned median is the median value of the combined sorted list formed by merging a and b
- The median value is within the range of the minimum and maximum elements of the combined list
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method MedianOfTwoSortedLists(a: seq<int>, b: seq<int>) returns (median: int)
    
Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - Both lists are sorted and of the same length
    
Dafny specification:
    requires a != null && b != null
    requires |a| == |b|
    requires Sorted(a)
    requires Sorted(b)
    
Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The median is the middle element of the combined sorted list of both lists
    
Dafny specification:
    ensures median == if (a.Length + b.Length) % 2 == 1 then
                        SelectMiddle(a, b)
                    else
                        (SelectMiddle(a, b) + NextMiddle(a, b)) / 2
    
*Note:* Since both lists are sorted and of equal size, the median is the average of the middle elements if total length is even, or the middle element if odd.

However, for simplicity, and given that both lists are sorted and of same size, the median of the combined list can be defined as the element at position (a.Length + b.Length) / 2 in the merged sorted list.

To avoid constructing the merged list explicitly, we can define a helper function to find the k-th smallest element in the union of the two sorted lists.

Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.

```dafny
method MedianOfTwoSortedLists(a: seq<int>, b: seq<int>) returns (median: int)
  requires a != null && b != null
  requires |a| == |b|
  requires Sorted(a)
  requires Sorted(b)
  ensures median == GetKthSmallest(a, b, (|a| + |b|) / 2)
{
    var totalLength := |a| + |b|;
    var k := totalLength / 2;
    median := GetKthSmallest(a, b, k);
}

// Helper function to find the k-th smallest element in the union of two sorted sequences
function method GetKthSmallest(a: seq<int>, b: seq<int>, k: int): int
  requires a != null && b != null
  requires 0 <= k < |a| + |b|
  requires Sorted(a)
  requires Sorted(b)
{
    if |a| == 0 then
        b[k]
    else if |b| == 0 then
        a[k]
    else
        var aMidIndex := |a| / 2;
        var bMidIndex := |b| / 2;
        if a[aMidIndex] <= b[bMidIndex] then
            if aMidIndex + bMidIndex >= k then
                // The k-th element is in the first part of a
                GetKthSmallest(a[..aMidIndex], b, k)
            else
                // The k-th element is in the second part of b
                GetKthSmallest(a, b[bMidIndex+1..], k - (aMidIndex + 1))
        else
            if aMidIndex + bMidIndex >= k then
                // The k-th element is in the first part of b
                GetKthSmallest(a, b[..bMidIndex], k)
            else
                // The k-th element is in the second part of a
                GetKthSmallest(a[aMidIndex+1..], b, k - (bMidIndex + 1))
}
```
